request.acceptance_criteria: Hegel property tests cover the five pure-logic areas and a reconciler state-machine model with at least the eight operations and five invariants listed; they run in go test and CI; any failure found is fixed or recorded with its minimal counterexample; the report says what PBT found and whether the model is worth growing
request.description:
Operator, 2026-09-27: trial Hegel (hegel.dev/go/hegel, beta; loads the Rust libhegel at run time, no cgo) in ticfac.

1. Pure logic first:
   - runconfig layering (5uo): tables merge field-wise, arrays replace, and the override cell applies last.
   - The Workers-AI-only rule (nwn/78v): no generated config ever resolves a cloud role, or a cloudflare-sandbox dispatch, to a model outside Workers AI. The rule is the provider namespace, not a model list.
   - forge CI aggregation: the latest run per check decides, and a skipped run never hides a failure. That was a real bug found 2026-09-26.
   - The findings parser: arbitrary JSON never silently loses a finding.
   - ClassifyRemote.
2. Then a first stateful model of the reconciler (Hegel's state-machine testing) over the existing fake tracker and fake runner.
   - Operations: dispatch; a worker settles succeeded / failed / with no report; the reconciler crashes and restarts; a transient remote failure; a write whose ack is lost; a same-wave merge conflict; a gate failure; a tick added mid-run.
   - Invariants (the lifecycle contract A1-A12): a live job is never redispatched; nothing closes behind a failing gate; the width is never exceeded; a cold restart reaches the same state; absorption stays bounded.
   - This week's bugs were all sequence bugs of this kind: the #50 resume order, the claim refusal that earned a rung, #53's unaskable remote, o82's lost-ack write.
Load hegel-skill (github.com/hegeldev/hegel-skill) when writing these. Wire libhegel into CI. Report what PBT found.
request.title: Property-test config layering, the Workers-AI rule and a reconciler state machine with Hegel (Go)
